narrative.h2: R&B video makes a feeling visible through light alone

sections.heading: What r&b looks like
sections.body: Modern R&B MVs are essentially short films with music. Lighting carries most of the emotional work: deep shadows, a single practical lamp, neon spillover through a window, candlelight. Color grades push warm and saturated or cold and desaturated, rarely neutral. Compositions are still — the camera is patient, often locked off or on a slow dolly. The artist is alone in frame more often than not, even when the song is about someone else. Wardrobe is texture-heavy: silk, leather, knit.

sections.heading: Reference points that actually work
sections.body: The Weeknd's entire Dawn FM and After Hours runs are master classes in mood-as-style. SZA's Snooze and Kill Bill prove narrative R&B still works when the lighting earns it. Frank Ocean's Nikes set the bar for R&B as experimental film. H.E.R.'s intimate performance videos show how to do it with restraint. Solange's A Seat at the Table visuals carry the art-direction ambition. The shared rule: mood over plot, always.

sections.heading: Prompting tip for Tunee
sections.body: Name your light sources explicitly and limit them to two or three. 'Single sodium streetlight through a sheer curtain, one practical bedside lamp, no fill' gives Tunee the constraint it needs to render mood. Keep the artist alone in frame unless a second person is critical. Long takes on the verses, slightly shorter on the hook — but never the rapid cutting of pop. Color grade should be decided early: 'amber warmth' or 'teal-and-magenta night' but never both.
